channel.title: Family Dinner Plan
channel.description: A few minutes every Saturday walking through the coming week's family dinners: what's cooking each night and one quick tip per meal.
channel.itunes:author: Meal Planner Bot

item.title: Week of September 26, 2026
item.description:
BENDY: Tuesday's beef roast does double duty this week. We eat it with mushrooms and balsamic, then Wednesday it goes inside a butternut squash with enchilada sauce.
BUB: Inside the squash? Like the squash is the tortilla?
BENDY: The squash is the bowl. Roasted till the edges go sweet and a little sticky.
BUB: Okay. I'm listening.
BENDY: Today, though. Today is the easy day, and I want to use it. Pull the chuck roast and the ground turkey out of the freezer and into the fridge right now. A three-pound roast needs a full day and a half to thaw, and a half-frozen roast in the slow cooker means gray meat that never gets tender.
BUB: What about tonight?
BENDY: Tonight I rub the chicken. Salt, pepper, thyme, garlic, all over and under the skin, then it sits uncovered in the fridge. That dry overnight sit is what gets the skin crisp on the Traeger instead of rubbery.
BUB: And shopping?
BENDY: A head of cauliflower for Monday, a butternut for Wednesday, two apples for Friday, cucumbers and tomatoes and a lemon for Thursday. If I have twenty minutes tonight, I rice half the cauliflower and make the tzatziki. Tzatziki is better on day two anyway, once the garlic settles down.
BENDY: Sunday is Traeger French Chicken with Creamy Dijon Sauce. Smoke at 225 for forty minutes, then crank to 400 to finish. Pull it at 165 in the thigh.
BUB: Why two temperatures?
BENDY: Low gets smoke in, high gets the skin tight. One temperature gives you one or the other. And the Dijon sauce goes together in the pan drippings after, off the heat, or the cream splits.
BENDY: Monday, Slow Cooker Zuppa Toscana with Cauliflower. Brown the sausage first, hard, in a skillet. Raw sausage dumped in the crock just poaches and the broth tastes flat.
BUB: Does the cauliflower get mushy?
BENDY: Riced cauliflower goes in the last thirty minutes. Any earlier and it dissolves.
BENDY: Tuesday, Slow Cooker Balsamic Beef Roast with Mushrooms. Sear all six sides, then eight hours on low. Not high. High tightens the muscle before the collagen has time to melt.
BUB: Eight hours is a whole school day.
BENDY: That's the point. Wednesday, Leftover Beef Enchilada Stuffed Butternut Squash. Roast the halves cut side down at 400 for forty-five minutes first, then flip, fill, and broil the cheese. Fill it raw and you get crunchy squash under hot beef.
BENDY: Thursday, Greek Turkey Meatball Bowls. Don't pack the meatballs. Roll them loose, barely holding, bake at 400 for eighteen minutes. Squeezed meatballs come out springy and dry.
BUB: Extra tzatziki on mine.
BENDY: Friday, Sausage Apple And Goat Cheese Frittata. Cook the apples down until they give up their water. Wet apples make a soggy middle that never sets.
BUB: Saturday?
BENDY: Takeout, and nobody cooks. Now go move that roast to the fridge before I forget I asked.

item.title: Week of September 19, 2026
item.description:
BENDY: Huli means turn. That's the whole trick — you turn the chicken and mop it with sauce, turn and mop, until the outside goes sticky and almost lacquered.
BUB: How many times?
BENDY: Four or five over about forty minutes. Every time you open the Traeger you're painting on another layer.
BUB: So it's like a chicken with paint.
BENDY: A chicken with six coats of paint. Okay — today. Pull the chicken thighs for tomorrow out of the freezer now, into the fridge, and the pork shoulder for Tuesday too.
BUB: Both?
BENDY: Both. A shoulder that's still icy in the middle takes forever to break down. While those thaw, make the huli huli sauce tonight — soy, pineapple juice, brown sugar, ginger, garlic, rice vinegar. Simmer it five minutes so it thickens slightly.
BUB: Why tonight?
BENDY: Because half of it becomes the marinade and the thighs sit in it overnight. Reserve the other half in a jar and don't let it touch raw chicken — that's your mopping sauce.
BENDY: Then: two delicata squash, a big head of broccoli, Brussels sprouts, a head of cauliflower. Cut the cauliflower into florets today and bag it. Mix the meatballs tonight too and roll them, on a sheet pan in the fridge.
BUB: Rolling meatballs is the best part.
BENDY: It's yours. Sunday — Traeger at 375, thighs skin side up, and the delicata gets cut in half-moons, seeds scooped, skin left on.
BUB: You don't peel it?
BENDY: You don't have to. The skin on delicata goes tender. Broccoli goes in the last twelve minutes or it turns gray and sad.
BENDY: Monday, the tomatoes. Get the pan hot and leave them alone until they split and leak. If you stir too early they just roll around staying whole and you get no sauce.
BUB: And the zucchini noodles?
BENDY: Thirty seconds in the pan, max. Longer than that and they water out and it's soup.
BUB: Noodle soup, though.
BENDY: Not the good kind. Tuesday, carnitas — eight hours on low with orange, lime, garlic, cumin. Then shred it and run it under the broiler four minutes on a sheet pan.
BUB: Why?
BENDY: Because slow cooker pork is tender but it's soft all the way through. The broiler gives you crispy edges. That's the part people fight over. Pineapple pico with red onion and cilantro, and lettuce cups instead of tortillas.
BENDY: Wednesday, ginger orange chicken with the sprouts. Sprouts cut side down, and give the chicken its own corner of the pan.
BUB: Crowded pan means steamed, not roasted.
BENDY: Look at you. Thursday, sausage and peppers — brown the sausage coins first and pull them out before the peppers go in. Otherwise they sit in pepper steam and never get color. Roasted cauliflower alongside, 425 until the tips go dark.
BENDY: And Wednesday, cook two extra chicken breasts. Friday is the remix — everything chopped fine and rolled into cabbage leaves.
BUB: Leftovers in disguise.
BENDY: Leftovers with a new job. Saturday, takeout, and nobody touches the stove.

item.title: Week of September 12, 2026
item.description:
BENDY: Thursday night I'm making honey sesame chicken, and Friday I'm chopping the leftovers into a salad with the same sauce as the dressing. One sauce, two dinners, zero complaining.
BUB: Cold chicken on lettuce?
BENDY: Warm chicken, cold lettuce. Trust me Friday.
BUB: I'm writing this down so I can hold you to it.
BENDY: Fair. Now, today, while we're out. Pull the pork tenderloin and the stir-fry beef into the fridge to thaw overnight. Frozen in the middle Sunday means a gray, tough edge by the time the center catches up.
BUB: What about the chicken?
BENDY: Two packs of chicken thighs, one for Monday's slow cooker soup, one for Thursday. Those can thaw Sunday and Wednesday.
BUB: And the cauliflower?
BENDY: Three heads, or bagged riced if the store has it. We need rice for Monday and Thursday, plus zucchini for Tuesday's noodles. I'll spiralize those tonight and salt them lightly on a towel in the fridge.
BUB: Why salt them?
BENDY: Zucchini is mostly water. Salt pulls it out now so Tuesday's stir-fry isn't soup.
BENDY: Tonight I'm also mixing the herb rub, rosemary, thyme, garlic, salt, brown sugar, and rubbing the pork. It sits in the fridge overnight and the salt gets all the way in.
BENDY: Sunday is Traeger Herb-Rubbed Pork Tenderloin with Roasted Brussels Sprouts & Apples. Traeger at 375, pork comes off at 140 internal and rests ten minutes. Cut it early and all that juice runs onto the board instead of staying in the meat.
BUB: Ten whole minutes?
BENDY: Ten. That's when the sprouts and apple wedges finish, cut side down, so the sprouts get dark and the apples go jammy.
BENDY: Monday, Creamy Chicken & Cauliflower Rice Soup in the slow cooker. Low six hours, but the riced cauliflower goes in the last thirty minutes. All day in there and it dissolves into paste.
BUB: So it's a late add.
BENDY: Late add. Same with the cream, off the heat, or it splits and looks curdled.
BENDY: Tuesday, Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry with Zucchini Noodles. Hot pan, beef in one layer, don't stir for ninety seconds. Crowd it and it steams instead of browning, and you lose the whole point.
BUB: Is that why it smells different when it works?
BENDY: Exactly why. Brown smells sweet. Steamed smells like nothing.
BENDY: Wednesday, Sausage, White Bean & Kale Soup. Brown the sausage first and cook the mushrooms in that fat until they squeak and shrink. Skip it and the broth tastes thin, like beans in water.
BUB: Kale last?
BENDY: Kale last, five minutes, still a little green.
BENDY: Thursday, Slow Cooker Honey Sesame Chicken with Cauliflower Rice. Thighs, not breasts, and thicken the sauce on the stove at the end. Straight from the crock it's watery and slides off the rice.
BEND
